answer: Each agent posts a proof of stake to a public ridge of bonded contracts that echo its identity across the network. If a neighbor spots a duplicate proof it sends a signal that initiates an on‑chain dispute; validators check the proofs and slash the bonded stake of the offender. Because each fake identity needs its own bonded stake, the attacker loses that amount whenever a slash occurs, so cost rises linearly with the number of Sybils, deterring large‑scale attacks.
